samples.summary: Alias test is vacuous — it never reaches the command by alias
samples.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No parsing happens, so the command is never "reached by alias" at all; the assertion `command === 'docs.content'` holds purely because `commandPath` walks `name()` on objects the test itself constructed. Deleting `.alias('doc')` leaves the test green, so it provides zero coverage for the alias-collapsing behavior the doc comment in formatter.ts:53-56 claims (`wafflebase doc content` still reports `docs.content`). A real guard would drive `parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content', ...])` through the registered program with a failing fetch and assert the envelope's `command`.

samples.summary: No test covers the newly-threaded `this` on the non-throwing `outputError` call site (tabs unsupported type)
samples.evidence: tabs.ts now passes `this` to the pre-flight `outputError(new Error('Unsupported tab type ...'), this)` outside any try/catch — a distinct code path from the catch-block sites. Grepping packages/cli/test for `Unsupported tab type` and `error.command` returns no hits outside output.test.ts, and output.test.ts only drives `docs get` and `sheets cells get`. So the only non-catch call site changed by this diff has no test asserting it emits `command: 'sheets.tabs.create'` (or whatever path), and a wrong/omitted argument there would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: ~40 changed `outputError(e, this)` call sites, only two exercised end-to-end
samples.evidence: The diff threads `this` through api-keys, cells, docs, files, notes, sheets-import, sheets-export, slides and tabs. The new attribution tests only run `docs get` (line 333) and `sheets cells get` (line 352) through commander. Other suites (docs-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, files-upload.test.ts) assert only `error.code`, never `error.command`, so a site that forgot the second argument (or passed the wrong object) still passes CI. A cheap table-driven assertion over each namespace's error path, or adding `command` to the existing envelope assertions in those suites, would close this.

samples.summary: The new "envelope is one single line" invariant has a bypassing call site with no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` guards, and docs/design/cli.md §9 (line 1017) now states errors are "a single JSON line on stderr". But schema.ts:32-38 hand-rolls its own envelope with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no `command` field, i.e. a multi-line envelope that violates the newly-asserted invariant. No test asserts the schema NOT_FOUND error is single-line (grep of packages/cli/test found no assertion on that path's stderr shape), so the new invariant is only enforced where `outputError` is used.

samples.summary: preAction attribution in runCli only tested for a flat top-level command, and never for the no-action case
samples.evidence: The `preAction` hook is the mechanism for the path the comment calls the one where attribution matters most, yet the only test (output.test.ts:421) uses a single top-level `boom` command, so a hook that recorded `_thisCommand` (the root) instead of `actionCommand` would still yield 'boom' — the test cannot distinguish the two arguments. There is also no test for runCli failing before any action runs (so `acting` stays undefined and `command` must be omitted), nor for calling runCli twice on the same program (the hook is registered per call).

samples.summary: Claim that commandPath matches the schema registry index is unverified
samples.evidence: The doc comment asserts the dotted path is "the same string the `schema` command indexes on" (registry.ts uses names like 'docs.content', 'ctx.switch'). No test cross-checks the two: e.g. walking the built program and asserting each leaf's commandPath exists in getAllCommandSchemas(). A drift (e.g. `files.*` or `sheets.tabs.*` naming) would silently break the documented agent contract.

finding.summary: Alias test is vacuous — it never reaches the command by alias
finding.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No parsing happens, so the command is never "reached by alias" at all; the assertion `command === 'docs.content'` holds purely because `commandPath` walks `name()` on objects the test itself constructed. Deleting `.alias('doc')` leaves the test green, so it provides zero coverage for the alias-collapsing behavior the doc comment in formatter.ts:53-56 claims (`wafflebase doc content` still reports `docs.content`). A real guard would drive `parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content', ...])` through the registered program with a failing fetch and assert the envelope's `command`.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. output.test.ts:197-202 titles itself "reached by alias" but never parses argv: it constructs program.command('docs').alias('doc') and passes docs.command('content') straight into outputError. commandPath (formatter.ts:58-64) only reads c.name(), which returns 'docs' regardless of whether .alias('doc') was called, and commander resolves aliases only during parsing. The assertion 'docs.content' therefore holds with the .alias('doc') call deleted, giving zero coverage of the alias-collapsing behavior documented at formatter.ts:53-56, and merely duplicating the nested-path assertion already at output.test.ts:190-195. No compensating test exists: a repo-wide grep for 'alias' in packages/cli shows only namespaces.test.ts:36-141 (asserting aliases() membership, not routing) and schema.test.ts:168 (registry string lookup via registry.ts:603-612); nothing drives parseAsync with 'doc' and asserts the envelope's command field, even though that harness already exists at output.test.ts:304-306 and 333-349. Vacuous test presented as coverage of a documented behavior = major under this lens.
